key_insight: OmniVideo-100K proposes a large-scale dataset designed to improve audio-visual reasoning by preserving structured links between sounds, visuals, and evidence chains. It moves beyond the usual clip-by-clip captioning pipeline to support more consistent, grounded QA over long videos.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key weakness in current audio-visual QA systems: decoupled audio and visual processing that breaks sound-source associations, plus short-clip segmentation that causes inconsistent descriptions across a video. It also targets the difficulty of long-text comprehension when generating answers from multi-modal evidence.
method: Build a dataset of 100K video examples with structured scripts and evidence chains for audio-visual reasoning.
Align audio and visual cues at a finer level so models can trace answers back to specific evidence rather than isolated captions.
Support longer-context reasoning by organizing information into coherent multi-step structures instead of independent clip summaries.
impact: For practitioners, this dataset can enable more reliable training and evaluation of models that need grounded audio-visual understanding, especially on long videos. It may improve consistency, traceability, and answer quality in real-world QA systems.

paper_title: OmniVideo-100K: A Dataset for Audio-Visual Reasoning through Structured Scripts and Evidence Chains
paper_authors: Xinyue Cai, Chaoyou Fu, Yi-Fan Zhang, Ran He, Caifeng Shan
